title: Mean and variance of a binomial
log: 2026-11-01T14:46:40Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point teaches the general definition of variance for any discrete random variable, not the binomial shortcut formulas E(X) = np and Var(X) = np(1 − p), so it is related but not the same idea.

draft.title: Mean and variance of a binomial
card: Suppose X is binomial with n trials and chance of success p on each trial. Then the mean is E(X) = np.
The variance is Var(X) = np(1 − p). The standard deviation is the square root of the variance.
Var(X) = 50 × 0.2 × 0.8 = 8. The standard deviation is √8, about 2.83.
draft.remember: Mean is np. Variance is np(1 − p), and the standard deviation is its square root.

a.q: X is binomial with n = 40 and p = 0.25. What is E(X)?
a.why: E(X) = np = 40 × 0.25 = 10. The value 7.5 is the variance, np(1 − p), not the mean.
a.clue: Multiply the number of trials by the chance of success.

b.q: A bakery in Ballarat finds 10% of its pies are underbaked. In a batch of 80 pies, X is the number underbaked. What is the standard deviation of X, to 2 decimal places?
b.why: Var(X) = 80 × 0.1 × 0.9 = 7.2. The standard deviation is √7.2 = 2.68. The value 7.2 is the variance, and 8 is the mean.
b.clue: Find the variance first, then take the square root.

check.summary: No problems found. Both answers check out: E(X) = 40 × 0.25 = 10, and SD = √(80 × 0.1 × 0.9) = √7.2 ≈ 2.68.
